sentences: Approximate all-pairs shortest paths permits a fixed additive error when edge weights lie in a bounded real interval.
The question asks whether undirected graphs admit nearly quadratic time if the matrix multiplication exponent equals two.
The source leaves this target unresolved even for a relatively large constant error.
Multiplicative approximation or unweighted exact distances do not automatically give the requested additive guarantee.
The project tests how close one can get to output-linear computation while preserving fine numerical distinctions between weighted paths.
